To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in CLL, MW, and MM the percentage of cells bearing surface Ig on their membrane is different from normal, but that the percentage of cells synthesizing Ig is not.
CLL, MW, and MM show different patterns of membrane and cytoplasmic Ig.

CLL is characterized by a monoclonal population of lymphocytes that have membrane-bound Ig but not cytoplasmic Ig, that MW is characterized by a polyclonal proliferation of cells with membrane-bound and cytoplasmic immunoglobulins, and that MM is characterized by a decreased percentage of lymphocytes with membrane-bound immunoglobulins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of surface immunoglobulin on lymphoid and plasma cells in chronic lymphatic leukemia, Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia, and multiple myeloma.
the detection of surface Ig in lymphocytes from patients with parapproteinaemia, especially with CLL, MW, and MM.
the detection of surface Ig in CLL, MW, and MM, and the results are discussed with regard to their diagnostic value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the paraproteinaemic states the lymphocyte population is characterized by the presence of a monoclonal Ig, which is bound either to the cell membrane or to the cytoplasm.

in CLL the cells are monoclonal and that the differentiation is intact, in MW the cells are polyclonal and the differentiation is intact and in MM the cells are monoconal and the differentiation seems to be disturbed.

the detection of surface Ig is of value in the diagnosis and classification of paraproteinaemic diseases, and that the direct method of immunocytochemistry can be used as a simple and rapid technique in the diagnosis of these conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, as far as the detection of membrane Ig is concerned, the direct immunofluorescent technique seems to give more information than the conventional method of indirect immunofluorescense.
the detection of surface Ig on lymphocytes in the blood and bone marrow is a useful method for the differential diagnosis of paraproteinaemias and lymphoproliferative disorders.
in CLL and MW, the cells are not only proliferating, but also maturing, while in myelomatosis there is no maturation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a surface Ig is not a prerequisite for the development of CLL.
the surface of the cell is not a good indicator of cell type.
the surface of a cell can be modified to control its interactions with other cells, tissues, and the environment.
